title: Generate and commit independent test vectors for yencoding
description:
Generate externally-derived test vectors for the yencoding crate and commit them as binary fixtures. These vectors are the oracle for all decode/encode tests -- they must NOT be derived from this crate own code.

WHAT TO GENERATE:
1. Single-part yEnc article: a short binary payload (bytes 0-63), encoded using Python arithmetic. Commit as tests/fixtures/single_part.yenc.
2. Multi-part yEnc article (2 parts of a 128-byte payload). Commit as tests/fixtures/multi_part_1.yenc and tests/fixtures/multi_part_2.yenc.
3. Article with prose preamble: a single-part block preceded by 3 arbitrary text lines. Commit as tests/fixtures/prose_preamble.yenc.
4. CRC mismatch article: correct encoding but crc32= field set to 0x00000000. Commit as tests/fixtures/crc_mismatch.yenc.
5. Truncated article: single-part block with the equal-yend line omitted. Commit as tests/fixtures/truncated.yenc.

HOW TO GENERATE (Python oracle -- do NOT use this crate):
  import binascii
  data = bytes(range(64))
  crc = binascii.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF
  out = []
  for b in data:
      v = (b + 42) % 256
      if v in (0, 10, 13, 61):
          out.append(0x3D); v = (v + 64) % 256
      out.append(v)

All fixtures must be accompanied by tests/fixtures/manifest.toml documenting: source tool/method, expected_decoded_len, expected_crc32 (hex), filename from header, is_truncated, expected_error (if any).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- tests/fixtures/ directory with at least 5 fixture files
- tests/fixtures/manifest.toml present
- No fixture was generated by this crate own encode() function
